 Democrat Jerry Williams leads Republican David Crane in Lake County sheriff race

 Democratic candidate for Lake County Sheriff Jerry Williams speaks during a forum held by the Miller Citizen’s Corporation on Wednesday, March 4, 2026. (Kyle Telechan/for the Post-Tribune) 
 By Maya Wilkins | Post-Tribune PUBLISHED: November 3, 2026 at 10:36 PM CST Getting your Trinity Audio player ready... As he led the Lake County sheriff’s race Tuesday night, Jerry Williams told the Post-Tribune his success belongs to the Lake County voters.
 “It belongs to all the voters that supported us, believed in us and gave us their confidence by where they cast their vote in the May primary,” he said, “and everyone who casted their vote during the general election and early voting.”
 Republican candidate for Lake County Sheriff David Crane speaks during a forum held by the Miller Citizen's Corporation on Wednesday, March 4, 2026. (Kyle Telechan/for the Post-Tribune) 
 According to unofficial Lake County elections results, Williams was leading Crane as of about 10 p.m. Tuesday night. Williams had 65% of the vote with 289 precincts reporting, while Crane had 35%.
 “I feel pretty good about where I’m at right now,” Williams said. “We’re excited about where we’re at in the process.”
 Williams has been in law enforcement for 33 years, with the most time spent with the Indiana State Police. He plans to use relationships built with the state police and other law enforcement agencies to benefit the department.
 On his first day, Williams plans to do a forensic audit of the department and third party audit of the commissary fund, he previously told the Post-Tribune.
 According to Post-Tribune archives, findings from a state audit showed the sheriff’s department improperly spent about $300,000 for charity or church donations, golf outings and travel costs. Indiana law says commissary funds can be spent on merchandise for the commissary, training, equipment or programs, among other items.
 He also plans to complete a comprehensive audit of the Lake County Jail and look at the possibility of hiring more correctional officers, saying the jail is understaffed.
 Williams plans to use experience with state police recruiting to guide recruiting at the sheriff’s department. He also wants to decrease overcrowding at the Lake County Jail.
 On Tuesday, Williams told the Post-Tribune that he’s thankful for the confidence of Lake County voters.
 “We were the right person at the right time to take the sheriff’s department,” he said.
 Crane previously said he worked with the sheriff’s department for 17 years, and he wanted to strengthen oversight, restore accountability, confront corruption and support Lake County’s youth.
 Crane was unable to be immediately reached for comment Tuesday.
 Crane previously said, if elected, he’d ask the Indiana State Board of Accounts to conduct an audit of the department and insist Attorney General Todd Rokita “prosecute any illegal activity found.” He also planned to use commissary funds for their intended purpose of reducing or preventing criminal activity.
 He also expressed concerns with jail conditions and said he planned to increase citizen involvement, including through a citizen oversight committee “to review every complaint made against any officer in the department,” and to start a school and children outreach program.
